name: Bergen
title: Hull Thickness Gauging Bergen | Offshore & Coastal Ships
description: Hull thickness gauging in Bergen for offshore vessels, shuttle tankers and coastal ships: UTM of hull structure, lay-up reactivation and pre-docking work.
h1: Hull Thickness Gauging for Offshore and Coastal Ships in Bergen
intro: Bergen is the hub of western Norway's maritime industries: the offshore supply base west of the city, the oil terminals at Mongstad and Sture, the coastal express route to the far north and a large fleet of aquaculture service vessels. Atlantis NDT mobilises a team from India to measure hull structure, tanks and piping on offshore vessels, shuttle tankers and coastal ships in the Bergen area, during yard stays, reactivations from lay-up and planned port calls.

highlights.p: When platform supply and anchor-handling vessels return from long lay-up in the western fjords, reactivation surveys need tanks, decks and piping re-measured. Corrosion during idle periods tends to concentrate in ballast tanks and seawater lines.

highlights.h: Shuttle tankers at Mongstad and Sture
highlights.p: DP shuttle tankers and crude tankers calling at the Mongstad and Sture terminals face oil-major vetting. CAP and renewal gauging of cargo and ballast tanks is done at docking, with deck and piping work possible alongside.

Well boats and feed carriers serving Norway's salmon farms pump seawater through their tanks and piping constantly. Well-boat tank structure and circulation lines are a gauging job that is distinctive to this coast.

port.h: Bergen's offshore, coastal and terminal traffic
p: Bergen sits at the centre of a coastline lined with offshore bases, oil and gas terminals and fjord shipyards. West of the city, at Ågotnes on Sotra, Coast Center Base serves North Sea installations with supply vessels, anchor handlers and subsea construction ships. Supply vessels working out of the base carry liquid mud, brine and base oil in tanks that corrode quickly once their coatings fail. To the north, the Mongstad refinery and crude terminal and the Sture terminal handle North Sea crude, and shuttle tankers and export tankers call at both. Product tankers, LPG carriers and coastal tankers move refined products along the coast from the region's terminals.

Bergen is also the southern end of the coastal express route that runs north to Kirkenes, and the city is one of Norway's busiest cruise ports in summer. Fjord ferries, fast passenger craft and coastal cargo ships work the surrounding sounds and fjords. Across the region, aquaculture has created a specialised fleet of well boats, feed carriers and service vessels supporting salmon farms, many of them Norwegian-built and maintained at the region's smaller yards. Many fjord ferries are now battery-electric or hybrid, and their conversions have added new foundations and penetrations to older hulls.

Ships stay long enough to gauge in Bergen for reasons specific to the region. Offshore vessels have repeatedly been laid up in the sheltered western fjords during downturns in North Sea activity, and reactivating them means a full survey with measurement of tanks, decks and piping that have stood idle. Shuttle tankers and offshore vessels go to yards in the region for maintenance between contracts. Coastal express ships and fjord ferries take their annual maintenance off-season. Each of these is a natural window for gauging, and Bergen thickness measurement demand follows that seasonal and contractual rhythm rather than daily cargo flows. The weather on this coast is a factor too: work on open decks is planned around frequent rain and wind, while tank and machinery-space work continues regardless.

Gauging in the Bergen area happens at offshore supply bases, at oil terminals, at lay-up berths in the fjords and at the repair and conversion yards along the coast. Offshore bases offer quay access, cranes and space for staging, which suits work on supply vessels and anchor handlers between charters. At the terminals, measurement on tankers is limited by cargo operations and the terminal's safety rules, so it is usually confined to deck and ballast spaces. Supply bases generally offer the tank-cleaning and waste reception services that offshore vessels need before tanks can be entered.

The fjords around Bergen and further north have many repair, conversion and newbuilding yards, from large offshore-vessel builders to small slipways maintaining fjord ferries and aquaculture boats. When vessels come out of lay-up, they are often taken to one of these yards for reactivation, and that is where most of the measurement is done. Which yard is used depends on the vessel, the scope and the owner's contracts, and we mobilise to the one selected. For laid-up vessels still moored in a fjord, access is by boat and the owner's lay-up crew prepares the spaces to be entered.
list: Coast Center Base, Ågotnes — tank, deck and piping gauging on supply vessels and anchor handlers between charters or before reactivation.
Mongstad crude terminal — deck, void-space and ballast tank measurement on shuttle and crude tankers alongside, subject to terminal approval.
Sture terminal — ballast and deck gauging on crude export tankers during loading, planned with the master and the terminal.
Lay-up berths in the western fjords — reactivation gauging on offshore vessels returning to service, including ballast tanks and seawater systems.
Fjord repair and conversion yards — docking-survey and renewal-survey gauging on offshore vessels, ferries and aquaculture vessels.
Bergen city quays — machinery-space piping and deck measurements on coastal express ships and cruise ships during calls or off-season lay-ups.

context.h: Norwegian regulation, ECA and offshore market context for Bergen
p: Norway is a Paris MoU member and Bergen sits within the North Sea SOx ECA. Offshore vessels and coastal ships in the region mostly burn distillate or run on LNG or battery-hybrid propulsion, so scrubber piping is mainly a concern on the crude and product tankers calling at Mongstad and Sture. Norway is an EEA state, so much EU maritime legislation applies through the EEA Agreement. For offshore vessels serving installations on the Norwegian continental shelf, operators' own requirements and Norwegian regulations add audit and verification steps beyond class, and documented structural condition forms part of the evidence vessel owners provide.

Market cycles shape inspection demand around Bergen more strongly than at a general cargo port. When North Sea activity falls, offshore vessels are laid up in the fjords; when it recovers, owners reactivate them in batches, sometimes after several years idle. Reactivation means checking for corrosion in ballast tanks, seawater cooling lines and fire mains that have been stagnant, and for coating breakdown where maintenance stopped. Shuttle tankers serving the Norwegian shelf are generally modern and well maintained, but their DP operations and long-term charters to oil companies bring strict vetting, which in turn drives CAP and renewal-survey gauging as they approach their third renewal survey.

jobs.h: Typical thickness gauging jobs in the Bergen area
jobs.p: Bergen work follows the offshore cycle and the seasonal maintenance windows of coastal and passenger ships. Scopes range from a few tanks on a supply vessel at a base to a full reactivation survey on a vessel that has been idle for years, and most are planned with the owner well before the vessel moves to the yard or base where the work will take place.
list: Reactivation survey gauging on an anchor-handling tug supply vessel: ballast tanks, chain lockers, stern roller structure and seawater lines measured before the vessel returns to charter.
Shuttle tanker inspection at a regional yard: cargo and ballast tank gauging for a renewal survey, with results prepared for the charterer's vetting review.
Well boat inspection: thickness of live-fish tank structure and seawater circulation piping, which see continuous seawater flow and frequent cleaning.
Offshore vessel thickness measurement at Coast Center Base between charters: deck plating, cargo rails and liquid mud tanks on a platform supply vessel.
Coastal vessel hull gauging during off-season maintenance: shell plating at the waterline, car-deck plating and ramps on a fjord ferry.
Pre-docking gauging of ballast tanks on a product tanker at Mongstad, used to scope steel renewal before the next docking.

logistics: Bergen Airport, Flesland, has connections through Oslo, Copenhagen, Amsterdam and other European hubs, and lies south of the city with road access to Sotra and the yards along the coast. Mongstad and Sture are reached by road north of Bergen. Terminals and supply bases are ISPS facilities with their own induction requirements, arranged through the ship's agent or the vessel operator; lay-up berths may need boat access, which the owner or agent organises. As Norway is in the Schengen area, the team travels from India on a Schengen visa, so reactivation work should be signalled as soon as the owner starts planning it.
vessels: Well boats and aquaculture service vessels

faqs.q: What should be measured when reactivating an offshore vessel from lay-up in the fjords?
faqs.a: Ballast tanks, fresh and drill-water tanks, chain lockers and seawater systems are the priorities, because stagnant water and reduced cathodic protection accelerate corrosion. Deck plating, cargo rails and towing equipment foundations follow. We agree the scope with the owner and class surveyor so that the reactivation survey and the gauging run together rather than one after the other.

faqs.q: Can you gauge a shuttle tanker at Mongstad or Sture?
faqs.a: Only deck structure, void spaces and ballast tanks can be considered while the tanker is at the terminal, and only if the master and terminal permit it. Cargo-tank gauging for a renewal survey or CAP needs the tanks gas-free and is normally carried out at a yard or during a planned off-hire period.

faqs.q: Do you inspect well boats and other aquaculture vessels?
faqs.a: Yes. Well boats circulate seawater through their fish tanks and piping, and the tank structure, sea chests and circulation lines are exposed to continuous wetting and cleaning chemicals. Ultrasonic thickness measurement of those areas, together with crack detection at pump and valve foundations, helps owners plan repairs at their next yard stay.

faqs.q: How quickly can a team reach Bergen?
faqs.a: Travel itself is straightforward through European hubs into Flesland, but the team comes from India and needs a Schengen visa, so timing depends mainly on visa processing. For reactivation programmes and docking surveys planned in advance this is rarely a constraint; for urgent work we tell the owner plainly when the team can realistically arrive.
